t: A 'Liability Only' (Act) private car policy does NOT cover:
o: Death of a third party pedestrian
Accidental damage to the insured's own vehicle
Damage to a third party's car up to Rs 7.5 lakh
Compulsory personal accident cover for the owner-driver
e: The liability-only policy covers third party death/injury, TP property damage and the owner-driver CPA; own damage is covered only under a package policy.

t: After the moratorium period in a health policy has been completed, the insurer can still repudiate a claim on the ground of:
o: Non-disclosure of a minor ailment in the proposal
e: Post-moratorium, no policy can be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation except for proven fraud, subject to policy limits and exclusions.

t: Which of the following is EXCLUDED under a Neon Sign insurance policy?
o: Theft of parts of the sign
Fusing or burning out of bulbs or tubes
e: The policy covers accidental external damage, fire, lightning, explosion, theft and RSMD; fusing/burning out of tubes and wear and tear are excluded.

t: Since the amendments made in 2022, the premium rates for compulsory motor third party insurance are notified by:
o: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in consultation with IRDAI
The Insurance Information Bureau of India
e: Motor TP rates are now notified by MoRTH in consultation with IRDAI under the Motor Vehicles Act framework; earlier IRDAI notified them directly.

t: An employee aged 30 years earning monthly wages of Rs 15,000 dies in an accident at work. The relevant factor for age 30 is 207.98. Compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Death compensation = 50% of Rs 15,000 = Rs 7,500 x 207.98 = Rs 15,59,850, which exceeds the minimum of Rs 1,20,000.

t: Under Section 164 of the MV Act (inserted by the 2019 amendment), the fixed compensation payable by the insurer in a hit-and-run-type claim not based on fault, in case of death, is:
e: Section 164 provides Rs 5 lakh for death and Rs 2.5 lakh for grievous hurt, replacing the earlier Section 163A structured formula.

t: A PA policy has a capital sum insured of Rs 20 lakh with TTD benefit at 1% of CSI per week and no further weekly cap. The insured is totally disabled for 10 weeks following an accident. The TTD benefit is:
e: 1% of Rs 20 lakh = Rs 20,000 per week x 10 weeks = Rs 2 lakh.

t: A 2.5-year-old private car suffers accidental damage. The approved repair bill includes metal parts Rs 40,000, plastic parts Rs 20,000 and windscreen glass Rs 10,000 (labour excluded). Applying standard depreciation on parts (metal 15% for 2-3 years, plastic 50%, glass nil), the amount payable on parts before excess is:
e: Metal 40,000 x 85% = 34,000; plastic 20,000 x 50% = 10,000; glass 10,000 in full; total Rs 54,000.

t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 (as amended), the minimum compensation payable in case of death of an employee is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Death compensation is 50% of monthly wages multiplied by the age factor or Rs 1,20,000, whichever is higher; for permanent total disablement the minimum is Rs 1,40,000.

t: The Bharat Griha Raksha policy for a home building can be issued as a long-term policy for a period of up to:
e: BGR allows the building to be insured for a long-term period of up to 10 years, with the sum insured automatically increased by 10% per year.

t: Which of the following is NOT a function of a bill of lading?
o: A certificate of insurance for the goods
Evidence of the contract of carriage
A document of title to the goods
e: A bill of lading is a receipt, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title; insurance is evidenced separately by the policy or certificate.

t: Under a Shopkeepers Package policy, which sections are generally compulsory for the policy to be issued?
o: Fire and allied perils on building/contents and burglary of contents
e: The fire and burglary sections form the core of the shopkeepers package; other sections (money, PA, PL, plate glass, neon sign, FG, baggage) are optional.

t: Insurers are required to cover mental illness in health insurance policies on the same basis as physical illness under:
e: Section 21(4) of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 mandates insurers to provide medical insurance for mental illness on the same basis as physical illness.

t: The 'Return to Invoice' add-on under a motor package policy pays, in case of total loss or theft:
o: The road tax and registration charges only
The difference between the IDV and the original invoice price, including registration and road tax
e: RTI bridges the gap between the depreciated IDV and the on-road price paid, so the insured can buy an equivalent new vehicle.

t: 'Extended maintenance' cover under a CAR/EAR policy indemnifies loss or damage during the maintenance period:
o: Caused by the contractor during maintenance visits only
Caused by the contractor during maintenance visits as well as damage attributable to faulty work during construction manifesting in the maintenance period
e: 'Visits' maintenance covers only damage caused while carrying out maintenance obligations; extended maintenance also covers damage originating from defects during construction.

t: Temporary Total Disablement benefit under a Personal Accident policy is payable for a maximum period of:
e: TTD is paid weekly (1% of CSI per week, typically capped) for the actual period of disablement, not exceeding 100 weeks in all.

t: Which of the following health insurance products operates on a 'benefit' rather than an 'indemnity' basis?
o: Hospital daily cash policy paying a fixed amount per day of hospitalisation
e: Benefit policies pay a pre-agreed sum on the happening of the event irrespective of actual expenses; indemnity policies reimburse actual expenses.

t: Under the 'money in safe' section of a Money Insurance policy, loss of cash is excluded if:
o: The safe is more than 10 years old
The loss occurs on a public holiday
The safe was left unlocked or the keys were left on the premises after business hours (unless the premises are occupied)
e: The key clause excludes losses from an unlocked safe or where keys were left on the premises, unless the premises are occupied by the insured or his employees.

t: A fire proposal for risk inception on 1 March is received along with a cheque on 5 March; the cheque is realised on 8 March. Under Section 64VB read with the Insurance Rules, the risk can attach from:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). When premium is paid by cheque, risk may be assumed from the date of receipt of the cheque provided it is subsequently honoured; cover cannot be backdated to 1 March.

t: In a co-insurance arrangement for a large fire risk, the leading insurer normally:
o: Issues the policy, collects the premium and processes claims on behalf of all co-insurers
Reinsures the whole risk with the other co-insurers
Is liable for 100% of the loss and recovers from followers later
Must hold at least 75% share of the risk
e: The leader administers the policy and claims; each co-insurer is severally liable only for its own agreed share, and the leader need not hold any particular minimum share.

t: For the AOG perils (lightning, STFI, subsidence, landslide) under the SFSP policy for sums insured up to Rs 10 crore, the standard excess per claim is:
o: 5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of Rs 10,000
e: Act of God perils carry an excess of 5% of the claim subject to minimum Rs 10,000; other perils carry a flat Rs 10,000 excess for such sums insured.

t: Under the 'aircraft damage' peril of the SFSP policy, which of the following is excluded?
o: Damage by articles dropped from an aircraft
Damage by an aircraft crashing into the building
Damage caused by pressure waves from aircraft travelling at supersonic speed
Damage by a helicopter making an emergency landing
e: The peril covers destruction by aircraft and aerial devices and articles dropped therefrom, but specifically excludes damage caused by pressure waves (sonic boom).

t: Under PMFBY, loss due to localised calamities such as hailstorm, landslide or inundation affecting an individual farm must be intimated within:
e: The farmer must intimate the insurer/bank/agriculture department within 72 hours of the localised calamity so that individual farm-level assessment can be carried out.

t: An insurer has an excess of loss treaty of Rs 1 crore in excess of Rs 50 lakh. A single loss of Rs 1.2 crore occurs. The reinsurer pays:
e: The cedant bears the first Rs 50 lakh (deductible); the reinsurer pays the excess, Rs 70 lakh, which is within the Rs 1 crore limit.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 provides that:
o: No risk shall be assumed unless premium is received in advance
Policies must be issued within 30 days of proposal
Proposal forms must be countersigned by the agent
Claims must be settled within 30 days
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VB requires that premium be received by the insurer, or guaranteed to be paid, before the insurer assumes the risk.

t: An Advance Loss of Profit (ALOP) / Delay in Start-Up policy covers:
o: Physical damage to the project under construction
Penalties for late completion imposed under the contract
Loss of anticipated gross profit of the principal due to delay in commencement of commercial operation caused by indemnifiable damage under the CAR/EAR policy
The contractor's loss of profit from idle plant
e: ALOP is a time-element cover for the project owner, triggered only by an insured material damage event under the underlying CAR/EAR policy.

t: The sum insured for equipment under Section I of an Electronic Equipment Insurance policy should be the:
o: Current replacement value as new, including freight, duties and erection costs
e: Like MBD, EEI requires the SI to be the new replacement value so that partial losses are paid without depreciation and average is avoided.

t: Under a cattle insurance policy, if the ear tag fixed on the insured animal is lost, the insured must:
o: Do nothing, as the tag number is on the policy
Immediately inform the insurer and have a fresh tag fixed at his own cost
Wait for the next renewal to re-tag
e: The 'no tag no claim' condition applies; the insured must get the animal re-tagged promptly and inform the insurer, otherwise a claim may be rejected.

t: A package of cargo is dropped and totally lost while being loaded onto the vessel. This is covered under:
o: ICC(B) and ICC(A) but not ICC(C)
None of the Institute Cargo Clauses
e: Total loss of any package lost overboard or dropped whilst loading on to or unloading from the vessel is a named peril under ICC(B), and is within the all-risks scope of ICC(A).

t: The standard personal accident product 'Saral Suraksha Bima' can be issued for a sum insured in the range of:
o: Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 1 crore, in multiples of Rs 50,000
e: Saral Suraksha Bima has a minimum SI of Rs 2.5 lakh and maximum of Rs 1 crore, in multiples of Rs 50,000.

t: If a motor package policy is not renewed within how many days of its expiry, the accumulated No Claim Bonus is forfeited?
e: NCB is allowed on renewal only if the policy is renewed within 90 days of expiry of the previous policy.

t: Under facultative reinsurance:
o: The reinsurer is bound to accept every risk ceded under the agreement
Risks are ceded automatically within agreed limits
Each risk is offered individually and the reinsurer is free to accept or decline it
e: Facultative placement is risk-by-risk and optional for both parties, unlike a treaty where cessions within the treaty scope are automatic.

t: Under a Consequential Loss (Fire) policy, 'gross profit' is defined as:
o: Net profit plus insured standing charges
e: Gross profit for CL purposes is net trading profit plus the insured standing charges (fixed costs that continue despite the interruption).

t: An annual fire policy with a premium of Rs 20,000 is cancelled at the request of the insured after exactly 4 months. Applying the standard short period scale (4 months = 50% of annual premium), the refund is:
e: The insurer retains 50% (Rs 10,000) under the short period scale and refunds the balance Rs 10,000; pro-rata refund applies only when the insurer cancels.

t: IRDAI requires every general insurer to maintain a control level of solvency ratio of at least:
e: The solvency ratio (available solvency margin to required solvency margin) must not fall below the control level of 150% (1.5 times).

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 Master Circular on health insurance, an insurer must decide on a cashless authorisation request within:
o: 1 hour of receipt of the request
e: The circular requires a decision on cashless authorisation within one hour and final authorisation for discharge within three hours of receiving the discharge request.

t: The arbitration clause in a fire or engineering policy can be invoked:
o: For any dispute including whether the insurer is liable at all
Only for disputes on the quantum (amount) of loss, after liability has been admitted by the insurer
Only after a civil suit has been filed
e: Arbitration under the standard clause is restricted to differences on the amount payable; disputes on liability itself go to the courts/ombudsman.

t: Under a fire declaration policy for stocks, the refund of premium at the time of final adjustment cannot exceed:
o: There is no limit on the refund
e: Premium is charged provisionally and adjusted on the average of the monthly declarations, but the refund is restricted to 50% of the provisional premium.

t: Under the Inland Transit (Rail or Road) Clauses, cover at the destination railway station or carrier's godown terminates on expiry of:
e: Inland transit cover continues until delivery at the consignee's warehouse or until 7 days after arrival at the destination station/godown, whichever is earlier.

t: Under PMFBY, the maximum premium payable by the farmer for annual commercial and horticultural crops is:
e: Farmers pay 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops; the balance actuarial premium is subsidised by governments.

t: Which marine arrangement is a stamped, legally enforceable contract with an aggregate sum insured that is progressively reduced by each declaration of shipment?
o: Floating policy issued under open cover
e: An open policy is a stamped policy for a fixed total sum against which declarations are made; an open cover is an unstamped agreement under which certificates/policies are issued.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: Under a Professional Indemnity policy issued on a claims-made basis, the 'retroactive date' is the date:
o: After which claims must be reported
From which the professional was first licensed
After which the act or omission must have occurred for a claim to be covered
e: Claims are covered if made during the policy period and arising from acts committed on or after the retroactive date (usually the inception of first continuous cover).

t: A warranty in a general insurance policy differs from a condition in that a breach of warranty:
o: Entitles the insurer to avoid liability even if the breach is unconnected with the loss
Only allows the insurer to charge additional premium
Has no effect unless the breach caused the loss
Can be waived only by a court
e: A warranty must be strictly complied with; its breach discharges the insurer from liability irrespective of whether it contributed to the loss.

t: Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd (AIC) was promoted by:
o: IRDAI and the Ministry of Agriculture
GIC Re, NABARD and the four public sector general insurers
The Reserve Bank of India and SBI
e: AIC was incorporated in 2002 with GIC Re, NABARD and the four PSU general insurers as promoters to take over crop insurance from GIC.

t: A CL policy has a rate of gross profit of 20%. Standard turnover for the indemnity period is Rs 50 lakh while actual turnover achieved was Rs 30 lakh. Ignoring ICOW and savings, the loss of gross profit payable is:
e: Reduction in turnover = 50 - 30 = Rs 20 lakh; loss of gross profit = 20% x 20 lakh = Rs 4 lakh.

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, the owner handling hazardous substances must contribute to the Environment Relief Fund an amount:
o: Equal to the premium paid on the compulsory policy
Equal to 10% of the sum insured
e: Along with the premium, an equal amount is paid as contribution to the Environment Relief Fund, used to pay relief when insured limits are exhausted.

t: The adjustment of general average is internationally governed by:
e: York-Antwerp Rules define what sacrifices and expenditures qualify as general average and how contributions are calculated; Hague-Visby and Hamburg Rules govern carrier liability.

t: In settling a motor theft claim on total loss basis, the insurer requires the insured to hand over, among other things:
o: The original RC, all keys and duly signed RTO transfer forms (Forms 28, 29, 30) along with a letter of subrogation
Nothing, as the vehicle is untraced
e: Since the insurer acquires rights over the vehicle if later recovered, it takes transfer documents, keys and subrogation/indemnity letters before releasing the IDV.
